text:
diane: heads-up: we got reports from customer 'primex' that SSO login flows intermittently fail during onboarding and SCIM provisioning shows duplicate create attempts. Seeing SAML validation errors in the auth-proxy logs and some missing audit.create rows for the same window (2026-05-10T02:34Z). anyone on call?

omar: can you paste the auth-proxy error? quick guess: assertion truncated by upstream proxy or max header/body size.

diane: paste from auth-proxy (trimmed):
```
2026-05-10T02:34:12Z ERROR saml: failed to parse assertion: invalid xml: unexpected EOF
2026-05-10T02:34:12Z WARN saml: signature verification skipped due to parse error
2026-05-10T02:34:13Z INFO scim-provisioner: attempted create externalId=primex-556
2026-05-10T02:34:13Z ERROR audit-publisher.kms: decrypt failed: AccessDenied
2026-05-10T02:34:13Z ERROR audit-publisher: publish failed, moved to DLQ
2026-05-10T02:34:14Z ERROR scim-client: HTTP 409 Conflict {"detail":"User already exists"}
```

lisa: interesting mix. "unexpected EOF" suggests the SAML POST payload got truncated. Which ingress are you seeing in front of auth-proxy? ELB + nginx?

diane: yes: ALB -> nginx-ingress -> auth-proxy (k8s). ALB access logs show a 200 but bytes_sent lower than expected for that POST. nginx error log shows `upstream sent too big header while reading response` earlier in the window.

omar: that `too big header` is usually nginx buffer size; but for SAML POSTs the payload is in body (base64 XML). If nginx treats a large cookie or header differently it can drop/trim and the POST body can be affected if proxy buffering misconfigured. Which nginx version? any recent config changes?

diane: nginx-ingress 1.14 upgrade rolled out yesterday with some default buffer changes. We also tightened cookie size via a new auth cookie for session state. Could be the upgrade changed `proxy_buffers`/`client_max_body_size` defaults.

rahul: two parallel problems here: 1) assertion truncation leads to parse error and we may retry or one worker succeeds and another fails -> duplicate create attempts at IdP (409). 2) audit-publisher KMS AccessDenied suggests RBAC/grant issue during the race window. Did we rotate the audit-publisher role or CMK policy recently?

diane: we rotated a few role ARNs last week for the provisioning namespace and there was a KMS grant refresh script that ran, but I don't see a grant for the audit-publisher new role in the CMK grants table right now.

lisa: remediation path: for the SAML truncation, patch nginx to increase `client_max_body_size` and `proxy_buffer_size` / `proxy_buffers` and re-run canary on the ingress. For the KMS AccessDenied, check `aws kms list-grants --key-id <key-id>` and compare grants vs the publisher role ARN; if missing, create a grant with Operations Decrypt+GenerateDataKey. Also replay DLQ to restore missing audit.create rows.

omar: quick commands to run from a debug pod:
```
# verify caller
aws sts get-caller-identity --output json
# list grants
aws kms list-grants --key-id abcd-ef01 --output json
# test decrypt as publisher principal
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://test.enc --key-id abcd-ef01 --encryption-context tenant=primex
```
Run those as the audit-publisher service account.

rahul: also check ALB access logs blob sizes for the SAML POST to see if truncation happened between ALB and nginx or inside nginx. If ALB bytes_sent equals content length of the POST then upstream likely truncated. If ALB reports fewer bytes, source client truncated (unlikely).

diane: ran list-grants as audit-publisher role; result shows an existing grant but principal is old role ARN. we rotated role last week and forgot to re-create grant. creating grant now with `Operations=["Decrypt","GenerateDataKey"]` and principal set to `arn:aws:iam::123456:role/audit-publisher-v2`.

lisa: good. For ingress, pinning back nginx-ingress to previous version avoided the truncation in our last incident, but let's patch config first. Add a canary config to set `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size: 16k` and `nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/client-max-body-size: 25m` and roll it for auth-proxy path only.

omar: after the grant and ingress config change, replay the provisioning DLQ and monitor for 409s. Also add a monitoring alert: spike in `saml.parse_error` and `audit-publisher.kms:AccessDenied` counts in a 1m window triggers a P1.

diane: infra-bot kicked off ingress canary (canary-id ingr-can-20260510-01) and I applied the grant. infra-bot: `DLQ replay job started for audit.publisher (job=dlq-replay-20260510-01)`.

diane: DLQ replay completed; audit rows for primex restored. after ingress canary churn, no more assertion parse errors in the last 20m. primex reports no further 409s.

rahul: add to runbook: when rotating publisher/provisioning roles, update CMK grants or use a key policy referencing the role. Add an ingress upgrade checklist to validate SAML POST sizes and verify `client_max_body_size`/`proxy_buffer_size` didn't regress.

lisa: I'll PR the nginx annotation canary as a default for SAML endpoints and add an e2e test that posts a large SAML response (simulate large attribute statements).

diane: postmortem summary in ticket: root cause = nginx-ingress upgrade decreased buffer/body defaults causing SAML POST truncation; secondary = role rotation without re-issuing KMS grant leading to audit publish failures; impact = intermittent SSO failures and missing audit rows; remediations = ingress config canary, re-created grant, DLQ replay, runbook updates, e2e SAML size test. closing once PRs merged. thanks team :thumbsup:
